title: Nonnegative Balance
statement: Implement `solve(start, updates)`. `start` is the initial balance. `updates` is a list of integers to assign, in order. A balance must be an int greater than or equal to 0. bool is rejected. On the first illegal start or update, return `error`. Otherwise return the final balance. The constructor uses the same check as the later assignments.
hints: Validate each update. Stop at the first failure.
type(value) is int and value >= 0 is the rule. True is a bool.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A property setter is the one place that can reject a negative balance, but only if the constructor also goes through the setter or the same helper.

editorial: A property setter is the one place that can reject a negative balance, but only if the constructor also goes through the setter or the same helper. Assigning to self._balance in __init__ and validating only in the setter leaves a back door. One helper used by both closes it.
